device: Read boot time VPD values from raw blob For security concern the kernel VPD driver (which exports /sys/firmware/vpd) does not allow key names with dot, but that is currently used by factory for manufacturing stage only. The VPD utility (/usr/sbin/vpd) supports names with dot, but reading firmware image from SPI is pretty slow on many systems, so we do want to read from the VPD cache from kernel driver. Since chromium:1686805, `vpd` now supports a '--raw' option that can decode from /sys/firmware/vpd/{ro,rw}_raw and we may use that in boot time for fetching VPD quickly. BUG=b:135048597 TEST=make test; Runs device.vpd.boot.GetAll() Change-Id: I037bdc4e5eaa5c7015dac3d8c9c4a0172f9b01b4 Cq-Depend: chromium:1686805 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1687737 Tested-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Wei-Han Chen <stimim@chromium.org>

device: led: probe the maximum value of brightness from ectool Previously in led.py, we assume the maximum value of brightness from the 'ectool led <name> <color>=<value>' command is 255. The actual maximum value may be different, e.g. 100. Using value larger than the maximum value is an unspecified behavior. On eve, it modulo the input value by the actual maximum value. In this case, the result is unwanted. This CL probes the maximum value of brightness using 'ectool led <name> query'. Also 'ectool led <name> <color>' set the brightness to 255, which always fails on devices with range check, e.g. nami. This CL makes brightness in LED.SetColor equal to 100 if not specified.
